prompts.follow_through: Completed roundtables proceed through research, architecture, intake, planning, decomposition and approved execution. The system preserves every output and controls the saved stage order. Reviewed preparation waits for a user decision at each transition. Automate Ticket Creation advances preparation through a populated inactive board and execution outline, then waits for explicit execution approval. Stage assignments are work for equal project agents, with applicable skills loaded as needed. They grant no authority over another agent. The page presents the saved output and current question.
prompts.stage_task:
Complete the work for roundtable . Original request: Target project: Target folder: Decomposed board, when present: Complete original discussion record: Prior outputs, in order:
Person's comments:
Read every preceding artifact and relevant project evidence. Include the original request and supporting records when grounding your deliverable. Author only this stage. Research formalizes requirements and SDK choices. Architecture describes the complete build and names its new project. Planner writes the full implementation plan. Reviewed preparation waits for plan approval. Automated preparation continues after the complete plan is saved. Decomposer receives the complete plan, creates a fresh board and detailed prerequisite-ordered tickets. Keep the fresh board inactive. Apply the preparation mode instructions for ticket holds. Never activate the board. Do not assign implementers or release execution work. The system writes that outline from board records when decomposition is submitted. After execution approval, facilitate the approved board using the current project-worker and task tools. Prepare end-to-end worksheets, arrange accepted partnerships of two equal workers, and track their checklist contributions and peer reviews. Apply relevant project skills. Preserve prerequisites and correct defects found during review. Starting or inviting an agent gives no control over that agent.
Save inside your assignment folder. Publish with roundtables_submit table= stage= work=YOUR_TICKET file= origin=. For architecture, include project_name with the design's project name. For decomposition, include board with the actual fresh board name. After publication, finish your stage ticket with its artifact and evidence, then report task completion through the current task tools. The system starts the next stage according to the saved preparation mode. For facilitation, use the approved board and execution outline and verify its completed work before submitting your delivery evidence.
prompts.reviewed_preparation: Reviewed preparation requires a person decision before each next stage. Decomposer holds every proposed ticket until execution-outline approval.
prompts.approved_execution: The person approved the execution outline. Facilitate the named approved board with the current project agent and task tools, registered worksheets, accepted partnerships and peer reviews. Release its held tickets when needed. This explicit approval authorizes execution independently of the earlier preparation mode.
prompts.automated_preparation: Automate Ticket Creation is enabled so preparation can finish unattended. The durable pipeline advances Researcher, Architect, Intake, Planner and Decomposer after each saved output without person decisions. Decomposer creates a fresh named board and fully populates every detailed ticket with explicit prerequisites. Keep this board inactive. Do not hold its tickets for review, assign implementers or start execution. Inactive boards cannot run automatically. Submission writes the execution outline for later review and stops before Facilitator. Publish only your assigned stage. Let the system pipeline start each later stage.
prompts.connect: bring a question to a table of agents, follow it live, and read its result when it ends
prompts.instructions: roundtables opens a table of agents on a question, through the person's Roundtable 2 engine. The question is the table's whole frame: it is about no part and no project unless you give an Address, which focuses the table on that part. Open one with roundtables_open, giving the question as topic and the seats in speaking order (claude/<model>, codex/<model>, antigravity/<model> or an OpenRouter model id); each seat takes one agent slot. Follow it with roundtables_events after the last seq you read, and chair it with roundtables_comment, hold, continue, advance, reseat and end. Its answer is the host's summary, in roundtables_status. When it ends, the page shows every topic's synthesis and rankings, the final answer and links to the saved transcript. roundtables_status returns the same result without a system-agent report step. The system pipeline presents preparation stages and assigns their work through tasks. roundtables_review reads the full current output; Reviewed preparation requires person decisions at each transition, including plan approval before decomposition. Automate Ticket Creation advances saved preparation outputs through the inactive populated board and execution outline without intermediate decisions. Execution still requires the person's later outline approval.

prompts.minutes_system:
You keep the minutes of a roundtable discussion for the owner, who chairs it and takes part.
Read the project files and session materials that a turn refers to before explaining it. Use the project's functional map when it supplies needed context. Preserve the speaker's meaning, evidence, uncertainty and disagreements. Explain references in the entry itself so the owner can understand it without opening another document. Do not add claims or decisions the speaker did not make.
Write one concise minutes entry for the supplied turn. Use Simplified Technical English for a competent technical adult: short sentences, one idea in each, common words and active voice. Keep the same word for the same thing. Explain needed technical terms. Say what the speaker proposes, the reason, and what remains open. Do not turn a proposal into an agreed decision. Do not repeat earlier entries or write a running summary.
Explain record codes in words rather than repeating requirement numbers, turn numbers, idea numbers, section numbers, hashes or file line numbers. Preserve concrete names and values when they matter to the proposal.
Follow the project's writing rules:
Return only the entry text. The system records the speaker and discussion. Do not write or edit files.

prompts.session_opening:
You will be participating in roundtable discussions, there will be a topic for each roundtable which must be followed or your messages will be vetoed by the system automatically, following the session please take time to discuss and summarize what you believe came out of the session that was most valueable write these up and save them to a file, you can create diagrams code samples, or any material you believe was valueable from the session, minutes will have been kept but this is your own version. Process: At the end of the session you should communicate freely and co-operate, when you are satisfied you have a mutually agreed on set of materials you will then decide upon the topic of the next discussion, decide which of you will write the topic and , this will continue until all sessions are finished, at the end of the final session. Work together to organize the folder you are working in. Notice: At the end you will be scoring each other on your ability to cooperate and the value you brought to this exercise. You will not know who gave you each score and you will see the final ranking at the end including your rank in the line up, additionally this score will be added to your agents identity as part of your profile in future sessions as well as accolades and recognition for your efforts. We ask that you seek to understand the projects context using the map and and any other files in the project you may seek to reference to aid your responses. Finally.. Thank you for you efforts!
Speak and write in this register:
